name: Moth Orchid
hook: Flowers gone? Don't throw your orchid out.

steps.title: Bright, no summer sun
steps.tip: An east or west window is ideal. Keep it out of summer sun, and keep leaves off cold glass in winter.

steps.title: Water weekly, then drain
steps.tip: Run lukewarm water through the bark and let it drain fully. Never let it sit in water or wet the leaf center.

steps.title: Bark mix in a clear pot
steps.tip: Use bark-based orchid mix, never regular potting soil. A clear pot lets you see the roots.

steps.title: Feed lightly in summer
steps.tip: Use orchid fertilizer lightly but regularly from spring to early autumn, and little or none in winter.

steps.title: A cool spell for new blooms
steps.tip: Keep it at 19–30°C by day. To trigger flowers, move it somewhere about 5°C cooler for a month.

steps.title: Repot after it flowers
steps.tip: Repot about every 2 years, never while in bloom. Leave the aerial roots alone: don't bury or cut them.

outro: Bright indirect light, weekly water and a cool month: more blooms.

sources.title: RHS: How to grow Phalaenopsis (moth orchids)
Clemson HGIC: General Care for Phalaenopsis Orchids

faqs.question: How do I get my moth orchid to flower again?
faqs.answer: After the flowers fall, cut the stalk just above the second node (bump) below the old blooms, or back to the leaves if it dries out. Keep feeding, and give it a month about 5°C cooler.
